kubernetes.label: Kubernetes
days: Day 1: Read the Kubernetes overview on roadmap.sh
Day 2: kubectl cheat sheet — pods, deployments, services
Day 3: Deploy a sample app locally with minikube or kind
Day 4: ConfigMaps, Secrets, and rolling updates
Day 5: Read one real job's k8s requirements and map gaps
Day 6: Troubleshoot a failing pod (logs, describe, events)
Day 7: Write 5 resume bullets from what you actually ran

aws.label: AWS
days: Day 1: AWS cloud practitioner map on roadmap.sh
Day 2: IAM, S3, and EC2 core mental model
Day 3: Deploy a static site or API to a free-tier service
Day 4: CloudWatch logs and basic cost awareness
Day 5: Read the JD's AWS list and mark must-have vs nice-to-have
Day 6: Terraform or console: one VPC sketch on paper
Day 7: Document what you deployed — no invented production claims

react.label: React
days: Day 1: React roadmap — components, props, state
Day 2: Build a list + form with hooks
Day 3: Fetch an API and handle loading/error
Day 4: React Router or Next.js app router basics
Day 5: Accessibility: labels, keyboard, one lint pass
Day 6: Match JD keywords to what your repo actually uses
Day 7: Ship a small public demo and link it

python.label: Python
days: Day 1: Python roadmap — syntax, venv, packaging
Day 2: Write tests for a small function (pytest)
Day 3: FastAPI or Django tutorial hello-world
Day 4: SQL + one ORM query you can explain
Day 5: Read the JD and list libraries you have vs lack
Day 6: Type hints and a linter on your project
Day 7: Honest GitHub README of what you built

sql.label: SQL
days: Day 1: SELECT, WHERE, JOIN on a sample dataset
Day 2: GROUP BY and window functions intro
Day 3: Indexes and EXPLAIN at a glance
Day 4: Model the JD's data in 3 tables
Day 5: Write 5 queries you could whiteboard
Day 6: PostgreSQL docs: constraints and transactions
Day 7: Put queries in a gist — no fake production scale

default.label: Core software skills
days: Day 1: Pick one JD skill you lack and read its roadmap.sh page
Day 2: Follow a freeCodeCamp intro for that skill (2 hours)
Day 3: Build the smallest demo that uses it
Day 4: Write what you did in plain language (interview answer)
Day 5: Re-read the JD — skip if it still wants 4+ years of that skill
Day 6: Apply to 1–2 junior-eligible roles that match what you have
Day 7: Follow up on anything you applied to 7 days ago
